general election.note: Usually plural, 'eleições gerais'. In Brazilian law it means federal and state elections held together, but the press uses it for the UK and other countries.

primary.note: Usually 'primárias' in the plural. In Brazil, party-internal selection is called 'prévias'; avoid that for US primaries.

runoff.note: Official Brazilian term. Plural: segundos turnos.

first round.note: 'Primeira volta' is the European Portuguese form; avoid it.

by-election.note: Brazilian electoral term for an election to fill a vacancy. The press sometimes uses 'eleição parcial' for UK by-elections.

special election.note: Standard rendering for the US. 'Eleição extraordinária' or 'eleição suplementar' are alternatives.

recall election.note: Also 'eleição de revogação de mandato'. The press often keeps 'recall' in italics.

contest.note: Can be 'disputa eleitoral'. Use 'pleito' for a formal election.

ballot measure.note: Umbrella term. For US measures the press also says 'medida submetida a voto popular'.

referendum.note: Brazilian law distinguishes referendo (vote after a law is passed) from plebiscito (vote before). For foreign votes the press uses both loosely.

proposition.note: Used as in 'Proposição 8' for California-style numbered measures.

retention election.note: No Brazilian equivalent; the press explains it as a vote on keeping a judge, often 'eleição de retenção de juízes'.

incumbent.note: Also 'ocupante do cargo'. A candidate seeking another term is 'candidato à reeleição'.

nominee.note: In Brazil, a party's candidate is chosen at a 'convenção partidária'. For the US, 'candidato do partido' is also common.

write-in.note: Voto in a name not on the ballot. The press often glosses it as 'write-in'. There is no Brazilian equivalent, since the electronic ballot box allows only registered candidates.

unopposed.note: As an adjective phrase, 'sem oposição' or 'eleito sem adversário'.

ballot.note: The paper ballot. The Brazilian electronic voting machine is the 'urna eletrônica'. 'Boletim' refers to the results sheet, not the ballot.

votes cast.note: TSE also uses 'comparecimento' for the number of voters who showed up.

valid votes.note: In Brazil these are votes for candidates and party labels, excluding blank and null votes.

invalid votes.note: Brazilian term for spoiled or annulled votes. 'Votos inválidos' is understood but less used.

blank votes.note: Counted separately from null votes in Brazil.

turnout.note: Its complement is 'abstenção'. Press also says 'taxa de comparecimento'.

registered voters.note: TSE term for people on the electoral roll. 'Eleitores registrados' is also acceptable for foreign contexts.

vote share.note: Also 'participação nos votos' or 'proporção de votos'.

margin.note: Full form: 'margem de votos' or 'margem de vitória'; also 'diferença de votos'.

swing.note: The press may keep 'swing' for UK elections. Full form: 'oscilação eleitoral'.

majority.note: More than half. 'Maioria' alone is often enough in context.

plurality.note: Also 'maioria simples' in some press usage. 'Pluralidade' is a rarer calque.

landslide.note: Also 'vitória avassaladora' or 'vitória por larga margem'.

constituency.note: For UK and EU usage. The press also uses 'distrito eleitoral'. 'Círculo eleitoral' is European Portuguese.

electoral district.note: General term. Brazil's own units are 'circunscrição', 'zona eleitoral' and 'seção eleitoral'.

district.note: Used as in 'distrito congressional' for the US.

ward.note: No exact Brazilian equivalent. The press sometimes keeps 'ward' and glosses it as a municipal subdivision.

precinct.note: US usage; the press may add 'distrito eleitoral'. The closest Brazilian unit is 'seção eleitoral', but avoid it for foreign precincts.

polling station.note: In Brazil, a 'seção eleitoral' is the voting unit within a 'local de votação'.

reporting unit.note: Descriptive rendering for any area that publishes results.

county.note: Used for US, UK and Irish counties.

municipality.note: Brazilian official term for the local government unit.

state.note: German Länder are usually rendered 'estado federado' or kept as 'Land' (plural 'Länder').

polity.note: Descriptive term for a country, state or territory that holds its own elections.

jurisdiction.note: In electoral contexts, 'circunscrição' is also used.

redistricting.note: Also 'redesenho dos distritos eleitorais' in the press.

legislature.note: 'Poder Legislativo' for the institution. In Brazil, 'legislatura' means the four-year term of a legislature, not the body.

lower house.note: In Brazil the lower house is the Câmara dos Deputados.

senate.note: Capitalize in names, as in 'Senado Federal'.

house of representatives.note: For the US. Brazil's equivalent is the 'Câmara dos Deputados'.

council.note: For Brazilian municipal bodies: 'câmara municipal' (members are 'vereadores').

officeholder.note: Also 'titular de cargo eletivo' for elected office.

independent.note: Brazilian law does not allow candidates without a party, so this applies to foreign contexts. 'Candidato avulso' is the Brazilian term in debates on independent candidacy.

coalition.note: For a governing coalition. In Brazilian electoral law, a joint electoral ticket is 'coligação'.

alliance.note: The Brazilian term for a joint ticket. 'Aliança' is also used.

open list.note: Used in Brazil for deputados and vereadores.

preference vote.note: In Brazil, 'voto nominal' is the vote for a candidate, as opposed to 'voto de legenda' (for the party).

constituency seat.note: Seat won in a single-member district.

overhang seat.note: German 'Überhangmandat'; the press often keeps the German term in parentheses.

threshold.note: Brazilian law also uses 'cláusula de desempenho'. Also called 'limiar eleitoral' for foreign systems.

quota.note: Brazilian legal term for the votes needed per seat. For STV, 'quota de Droop' is used.

first past the post.note: The press often glosses 'first past the post' in parentheses.

ranked-choice voting.note: Also 'votação por ordem de preferência'. Full form for US: 'votação por escolha ranqueada'.

mixed-member proportional.note: Also 'representação proporcional mista'; abbreviation MMP is used.

D'Hondt method.note: Brazil uses a similar highest-averages step ('sobras') after the quociente eleitoral.

Sainte-Laguë method.note: Spelled as in French, with the diaeresis.

count.note: The general word for counting is 'contagem' or 'apuração'.

certified.note: In Brazil, the electoral court 'homologa' the result, and the winner is 'diplomado'. US 'certified' is also rendered 'certificado'.

preliminary results.note: 'Resultados parciais' is also common in Brazilian press for partial counts.

called.note: Used when a race is declared won; the verb is 'projetar'.

too close to call.note: Press phrase: 'disputa apertada demais para projetar vencedor'.

reporting.note: Share counted: 'percentual apurado'. In Brazil, urnas report quickly, so this is mainly for foreign contexts.

absentee ballot.note: No Brazilian equivalent. Brazilian voters away from home vote at special points or abroad.

mail-in ballot.note: Also 'voto pelo correio'. Not used in Brazil.

flip.note: A seat that changes party; the verb is 'virar'.

gain.note: A seat won from another party. Press also says 'conquista'.

gerrymander.note: The English term is normally kept in Brazilian press and treated as a masculine noun, often glossed as 'manipulação de distritos eleitorais'.

electoral college.note: Capitalized when it refers to the US body.

delegate.note: Brazilian party conventions also have delegados.

convention.note: In Brazil, the formal party meeting that selects candidates.

roll call.note: At US conventions, the 'chamada nominal dos estados'.

changeset.note: Technical term for a reviewed batch of edits.

workbench.note: Software term; 'ambiente de trabalho' is an alternative.
